strongest_bounded_proposition: Ancient South Arabian epigraphy demonstrates subordinate, captive and enslaved statuses, including later Hadhramitic attestations, but the packet does not securely establish Hadhramaut slavery at c.500 BCE.
strongest_unsupported_proposition: Do not move second-/third-century CE Hadhramitic status evidence backward seven centuries.
territorial_practice_summary: Ancient South Arabian slavery/subordination is a valid regional context; target-specific 500 BCE practice remains unresolved.
terminology_category_qualification: ʿbd, ʾdm, captive and servant terms require contextual reading.
temporal_scope_precision: The directly cited Hadhramitic status inscription is late second–third century CE, much later than the anchor.
inference_extent: No inference beyond the stated target/evidence locus.
language_access_limitations: English-accessible research packet only; non-English and non-digitized scholarship was not exhaustively searched.

sources.title: Slavery in First Millennium Arabia: Epigraphy and the Qurʾān
sources.author: Valentina A. Grasso

unresolved_issues: Temporal gap between anchor and direct Hadhramitic status evidence.
